newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares bow to listless holiday mood.
newsitem.headline: German shares bow to listless holiday mood.

text.p: German shares traded just lower on Wednesday afternoon as the approach of Thursday's Ascension Day holiday sapped investor interest.
"Nobody wants to make a bet right now," said a Frankfurt dealer. "This is not a day for testing any records."
The IBIS DAX index was down 6.42 points at 3,542.10 points at 1302 GMT, having eased slightly from the DAX's bourse close level of 3,551.98 points.
Blue chip shares were mixed, amid good demand for airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG and utility Veba AG offset by declines on drugs and chemicals group Bayer.
June DTB DAX futures were down 6.5 points at 3,548.5.
Lufthansa traded up 56 pfennigs at 27.05 marks on significant volumes after news of a 20 million mark profit in the first quarter of 1997 -- the first in its history.
News of an 18.7 percent rise in first quarter operating profit also boosted Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, which was up 2.06 marks at 74.45.

Bayer fell 2.10 marks to 66.60 marks on news a final settlement would soon be reached forcing it to pay some 460 million marks to friends and relatives of more than than 6,000 hemophiliacs infected with Aids through tainted blood products.
Utility Veba remained in demand after an upbeat first quarter earnings report on Tuesday.
The stock was up 1.51 marks at 94.43 marks in afternoon trade.
Dealers said expectations of profit-taking on Wall Street might likely weigh on the broad German market in later electronic trade but downplayed the immediate significance of this.
"We may not see a real trend until next week now," said a trader.
